acceptance_criteria: python3 -m ct.export_transitions --dry-run exits 0 and prints a count summary to stderr
python3 -m ct.export_transitions prints only JSON lines, each parseable by json.loads, with review_required true and accepted null
the module imports ledger helpers from ct.ct instead of duplicating event parsing
intent: Create a NEW module ct/export_transitions.py (stdlib only, Python 3.12+) for the continuity tool. It reads the local ledger the same way ct/ct.py does (import and reuse ct.ct's existing ledger-loading helpers rather than re-implementing parsing; look at how cmd_recall and cmd_stats iterate events) and emits one JSON object per line on stdout, one per work item (events of type work_item.opened), in this shape: {"schema": "operational_transition.v0", "trajectory_id": <work item id>, "transition_type": "work_item", "cutoff_T": <ISO timestamp of the work_item.opened event>, "source": {"repo_id": <repo from the opening event>, "objective": <objective text>}, "context_at_T": {"receipts": <count of receipt.recorded events whose work field equals this work item>, "checkpoints": <count of checkpoint.observed events linked to it>, "observations": <count of observation.recorded events about it>}, "target": {"status": <latest status.asserted value for it, or null>}, "review_required": true, "accepted": null}. Provide a main() with argparse: --ledger <path> (default: the same ledger path ct.ct resolves from its config) and --dry-run (print a one-line count summary to stderr instead of records). Keep the module under 200 lines, no third-party imports, no writes to disk.
